correctness.rationale: The precisely defined Cayley graph has 16 vertices, 48 edges and strong-regularity common-neighbor count 2. An independently reconstructed augmented Alexander dual has face counts (1,16,120,176,60) with no five-element faces. Each of its 60 tetrahedra has a private triangle, permitting 60 exact elementary collapses. The residual two-complex has a complete 1-skeleton and 116 triangles. The integral signed boundary projected onto the 105 non-spanning-tree edges is reduced by 105 explicitly constructed unimodular unit pivots to [I_105 | 0_105x11], proving H_2=Z^11 and H_1=0 without torsion. The duality shift n-i-3=2 gives degree 11. Containing the full ten-skeleton ensures nine-connectivity, and H_10=0 promotes to ten-connectivity by Hurewicz. Representing H_11 generators and applying homological Whitehead yields the stated wedge homotopy equivalence. The exact package checker was executed, not inferred from finite-field samples.

value.rationale: The Shrikhande graph and the 4x4 rook graph are the two natural strongly regular graphs with identical parameters (16,6,2,2); ordinary three-cut homotopy is a structurally meaningful graph invariant capable of distinguishing them. Unlike an arbitrary enumeration, the theorem identifies a complete integral homotopy type and proves torsion-freeness, a degree shift and nonshellability. Its rank 11 differs materially from the known rook rank 27. This exact natural case is a useful boundary to general graph-parameter-based topology expectations without requiring an invented downstream application or a general classification.
